CausalChain: Overexpression of lncRNA (e.g., RP11-156p1.3) in HCC -> drives immune evasion by reducing antigen presentation and increasing regulatory T cell infiltration -> establishes an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment -> targeted CRISPR/Cas9 via liver-directed nanoparticles can knock out the lncRNA -> reversal of immune suppression and increased tumor antigenicity -> enhanced efficacy of PD-1/PD-L1 blockade -> improved antitumor immune response and tumor regression in HCC
Hypothesis: Targeted CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of immunosuppressive lncRNAs, such as RP11-156p1.3, using liver-specific nanoparticle delivery, combined with PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint inhibition, will reprogram the HCC tumor microenvironment and overcome immune evasion, thereby enhancing antitumor efficacy.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains difficult to treat due in part to its immunosuppressive microenvironment and resistance to conventional therapies. Emerging evidence indicates that certain long non‐coding RNAs (lncRNAs) contribute to immune evasion by modulating antigen presentation and promoting regulatory cell infiltration. In this context, we propose a novel combinatorial strategy that couples nanoparticle‐mediated CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing of a specific immunosuppressive lncRNA with immune checkpoint blockade. By selectively disrupting lncRNAs such as RP11‐156p1.3, it may be possible to reprogram the tumor milieu to enhance T cell infiltration and responsiveness. When combined with inhibitors targeting PD‑1/PD‑L1, this dual approach could overcome intrinsic immune resistance and improve therapeutic outcomes in HCC.
